              - cell "← 2023 (old format) 2029 →" [ref=e304]

          - paragraph
            - StaticText "The "
            - StaticText "2025 FIFA Club World Cup"
            - StaticText ", also marketed as "
            - StaticText "FIFA Club World Cup 25"
            - StaticText ", was the 21st edition of the "
            - link "FIFA Club World Cup" [ref=e94]
            - StaticText ", an international club "
            - link "soccer" [ref=e95]
            - StaticText " competition organized by "
            - link "FIFA" [ref=e96]
            - StaticText ". This was also the first edition under the new expanded format. The tournament was held in the "
            - link "United States" [ref=e97]
            - StaticText " from June 14 to July 13, 2025, and featured 32 teams. The expanded format included the continental champions from the past four years as well as additional qualified teams. "
            - link "Chelsea" [ref=e98]
            - StaticText " won the tournament, defeating "
            - link "Paris Saint-Germain" [ref=e99]
            - StaticText " 3–0 in the "
            - link "final" [ref=e100]
            - StaticText " and becoming the inaugural world champions under the expanded format."
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "The revised structure was modeled more closely on the "
            - link "FIFA World Cup" [ref=e101]
            - StaticText " as a quadrennial world championship, replacing the annual seven-team format used between 2000 and 2023. It featured the winners of each continent's top club competition from 2021 to 2024, except for a single entry from "
            - link "Oceania" [ref=e102]
            - StaticText ". Additional slots were awarded to clubs from Europe and South America based on rankings across the same four-year period. "
            - link "Manchester City" [ref=e103]
            - StaticText ", who won the final edition under the previous format in "
            - link "2023" [ref=e104]
            - StaticText ", entered as the technical title holders but were eliminated in the round of 16 by "
            - link "Al Hilal" [ref=e105]
            - StaticText "."
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "FIFA first announced the expanded format in March 2019, originally selecting China to host the inaugural edition in 2021. This was later postponed due to the global "
            - link "COVID-19 pandemic" [ref=e106]
            - StaticText ". In February 2023, FIFA confirmed the allocation of qualification slots among confederations, and four months later announced the United States as the new host nation. Alongside this expansion, FIFA also introduced the "
            - link "FIFA Intercontinental Cup" [ref=e107]
            - StaticText ", an annual tournament based on the previous Club World Cup format."
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "The expansion of the tournament drew varied responses, with some concerns raised by the players' union "
            - link "FIFPRO" [ref=e108]
            - StaticText " and the "
            - link "World Leagues Forum" [ref=e109]
            - StaticText " regarding potential effects on fixture schedules and player welfare. Ticket sales were managed using "
            - link "dynamic pricing" [ref=e110]
            - StaticText ", which was later adjusted for several matches to boost attendance. International broadcasting rights were secured by streaming service "
            - link "DAZN" [ref=e111]
            - StaticText ", which sublicensed coverage to other networks. A total of $1 billion in "
            - link "prize money" [ref=e112]
            - StaticText " was distributed among the 32 clubs, including solidarity payments and allocations by confederation."
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "It was the first major FIFA tournament since the "
            - link "1978 FIFA World Cup" [ref=e113]
            - StaticText " not to feature a "
            - link "penalty shootout" [ref=e114]
            - StaticText "."
        - region "Background and format" [ref=e14]
          - generic
            - heading "Background and format" [level=2, ref=e115]
            - link "edit" [ref=e116]
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "Since its return from hiatus in 2005, the "
            - link "FIFA Club World Cup" [ref=e117]
            - StaticText " had been held annually in December and was limited to the winners of continental club competitions."
            - superscript
              - link "[1]" [ref=e305]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "1"
                  - StaticText "]"
            - StaticText " As early as late 2016, "
            - link "FIFA president" [ref=e118]
            - StaticText " "
            - link "Gianni Infantino" [ref=e119]
            - StaticText " suggested expanding the Club World Cup to 32 teams beginning in 2019 and rescheduling it to June/July to be more balanced and attractive to broadcasters and sponsors."
            - superscript
              - link "[2]" [ref=e306]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "2"
                  - StaticText "]"
            - StaticText " In late 2017, FIFA discussed proposals to expand the competition to 24 teams and have it be played every four years starting in 2021, replacing the "
            - link "FIFA Confederations Cup" [ref=e120]
            - StaticText "."
            - superscript
              - link "[3]" [ref=e307]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "3"
                  - StaticText "]"

            - StaticText " meeting in "
            - link "Miami" [ref=e122]
            - StaticText "."
            - superscript

          - paragraph
            - StaticText "On June 23, 2023, FIFA confirmed that the United States would host the 2025 tournament as a prelude to the "
            - link "2026 FIFA World Cup" [ref=e125]
            - StaticText "."
            - superscript

                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "10"

            - StaticText " The 32 teams were divided into eight groups of four teams, with the top two teams in each group qualifying to the knockout stage."
            - superscript
              - link "[11]" [ref=e315]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "11"
                  - StaticText "]"

            - StaticText " between "

          - paragraph
            - StaticText "In January 2024, it was reported that the tournament would mainly take place on the "
            - link "East Coast" [ref=e130]
            - StaticText " to be closer to European broadcasters and viewers while also avoiding conflicts with the "
            - link "2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup" [ref=e131]

          - region "Trophy" [ref=e56]
            - generic
              - heading "Trophy" [level=3, ref=e318]
              - link "edit" [ref=e319]
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "FIFA unveiled a newly designed trophy created by "
              - link "Tiffany & Co." [ref=e320]
              - StaticText " for the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup. Made from pure "
              - link "24-karat" [ref=e321]
              - StaticText " "
              - link "gold" [ref=e322]
              - StaticText ", the trophy's design drew inspiration from pioneering maps, the periodic table, astronomy, and the "
              - link "Voyager Golden Record" [ref=e323]
              - StaticText ". It featured laser-engraved details including a world map, the names of all 211 FIFA member associations, descriptions of football, and inscriptions in 13 languages, including "
              - link "braille" [ref=e324]
              - StaticText "."
              - superscript
                - link "[14]" [ref=e567]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "14"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " The trophy weighs approximately "
              - StaticText "5 kilograms (11"
              - StaticText "lb) and is valued between €200,000 or US$230,000."
              - superscript

                  - generic

                    - StaticText "15"

              - link "Oval Office" [ref=e326]

            - StaticText "If a club won two or more seasons of its confederation's top club competition, additional teams determined club rankings over the four-year period. Furthermore, a restriction of two clubs per association was applied, with the exception of champion clubs if more than two clubs from the same association won their confederation's top club competition. The calculation method for the four-year club rankings within each confederation was based on the teams' performance in their respective continental tournaments during seasons completed between 2021 and 2024."

            - paragraph
              - StaticText "FIFA compiled the draw pots as follows, with teams ranked within each confederation based on FIFA's club ranking system:"
              - superscript
                - link "[19]" [ref=e591]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "19"
                    - StaticText "]"
            - list
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pot 1: The four top-ranked teams from both UEFA and CONMEBOL"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pot 2: The remaining eight teams from UEFA"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pot 3: The two top-ranked teams from each of AFC, CAF and CONCACAF, and the remaining two teams from CONMEBOL"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pot 4: The remaining teams from AFC, CAF, CONCACAF, OFC and host country"
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "In the draw, teams from the same confederation could not be drawn into the same group except for UEFA teams, for which there was at least one and no more than two per group. Additionally, teams from the same national association could be drawn into the same group."
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "To maintain competitive balance, two separate pathways of four groups were established for the knockout stage. They were composed as follows:"
            - list
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pathway 1: Winners of Groups A, C, E, and G, paired with the runners-up of Groups B, D, F, and H"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "Pathway 2: Winners of Groups B, D, F, and H, paired with the runners-up of Groups A, C, E, and G"
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "Given these pathways, UEFA and CONMEBOL teams faced the following constraints in the draw:"
            - list
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "UEFA teams ranked 1–2, and CONMEBOL teams ranked 1–2 were allocated to separate pathways, prevented from meeting until the semifinals should they finish in the same relative position in the top two of their respective groups"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "UEFA teams ranked 3–4, and CONMEBOL teams ranked 3–4, were allocated to separate pathways, prevented from meeting until the semifinals should they finish in the same relative position in the top two of their respective groups"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "UEFA teams ranked 1–4 were drawn into groups that would prevent them from meeting until the semifinals, should they finish in the same relative position in the top two of their respective groups, not necessarily win them."
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "CONMEBOL teams ranked 1–4 were drawn into groups that would prevent them from meeting until the semifinals, should they finish in the same relative position in the top two of their respective groups, not necessarily win them."
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "UEFA teams ranked 5–8 were drawn into groups with CONMEBOL teams ranked 1–4"
              - listitem [level=1]
                - ListMarker "• "
                - StaticText "UEFA teams ranked 9–12 were drawn into groups with UEFA teams ranked 1–4"
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "As teams from the host country and for scheduling purposes, "
              - link "Inter Miami" [ref=e355]
              - StaticText " and the "
              - link "Seattle Sounders" [ref=e356]
              - StaticText " were drawn into position 4 of Groups A and B, respectively. Consequently, teams drawn into Groups A and B were allocated to the position corresponding to their draw pot."
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "The draw started with Pot 1 and ended with Pot 4, with each team selected then allocated into the first available group alphabetically, based on the draw constraints. For Groups C to H, the position for the team within the group was then drawn (for the purpose of the match schedule), with the Pot 1 teams automatically drawn into position 1 of each group."

          - region "Training bases" [ref=e60]
            - generic
              - heading "Training bases" [level=3, ref=e364]
              - link "edit" [ref=e365]
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "According to a report from "
              - link "The Athletic" [ref=e593]
              - StaticText ", FIFA designated sites in host cities for team training bases, with priority given to clubs that had more matches in the area. Clubs were permitted to independently negotiate with other facility owners and operators, including several college athletic programs, to secure their own base. Several facilities were also designated by FIFA for use later in the tournament by qualified teams in the knockout rounds."

        - region "Schedule" [ref=e19]
          - generic
            - heading "Schedule" [level=2, ref=e164]
            - link "edit" [ref=e165]
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "On December 17, 2023, FIFA announced the tournament would take place from June 15 to July 13, 2025."
            - superscript
              - link "[12]" [ref=e368]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "12"
                  - StaticText "]"
            - StaticText " Prior to the draw, only the date and venue of the opening match (involving "
            - link "Inter Miami" [ref=e166]
            - StaticText ") and final was confirmed, along with the venue for the group stage matches of the "
            - link "Seattle Sounders" [ref=e167]
            - StaticText ". The full match schedule with venues and kickoff times was finalized and published on December 7, 2024, following the draw."
            - superscript
              - link "[45]" [ref=e369]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "45"
                  - StaticText "]"
            - StaticText " The start date of the tournament was altered, with the tournament beginning one day earlier on June 14. The schedule was created taking into account factors such as \"sporting and player-centric criteria, local and traveling fans and global broadcast considerations\"."
            - superscript
              - link "[33]" [ref=e370]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "33"
                  - StaticText "]"

            - link "2025 FIFA Club World Cup squads" [ref=e170]
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "Each club was required to name a provisional squad of between 26 and 50 players for the tournament. From June 1 to 10, 2025, the member associations of all participating clubs implemented an extraordinary transfer window to allow for the registration of newly signed players. Clubs were required to name their final squads of between 26 and 35 players, including at least three goalkeepers, by June 10."
            - superscript
              - link "[46]" [ref=e371]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "46"
                  - StaticText "]"
            - StaticText " During the competition, clubs could make "
            - link "limited changes" [ref=e171]
            - StaticText " to their final lists from June 27 to July 3, should the club's member association have a transfer window open during this period, though no player could appear for two clubs during the tournament."

        - region "Prize money" [ref=e26]
          - generic
            - heading "Prize money" [level=2, ref=e200]
            - link "edit" [ref=e201]
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "The distribution model split a total prize pool of US$1 billion between the 32 participating clubs. The winner of the tournament was awarded up to US$125 million, marking a significant increase in financial rewards compared to previous editions. In addition to the prize money for the participating teams, a solidarity investment program had a target of an additional US$250 million being provided to club football across the world."
            - superscript
              - link "[117]" [ref=e424]
                - generic
                  - StaticText "["
                  - StaticText "117"
                  - StaticText "]"
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "The distribution model for the 2025 edition was as follows:"
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "Sporting performance pillar (US$475 million):"
            - StaticText " Increasing payouts based on performance in the tournament."
          - list
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Group stage (three matches): + $2.0 million per win; + $1.0 million draw"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Round of 16: + $7.5 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Quarterfinal: + $13.125 million"

              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Semifinal: + $21.0 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Finalist: + $30.0 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Winner: + $40.0 million"
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "Participation pillar (US$525 million):"
            - StaticText " Guaranteed payments to all 32 clubs (amounts are per club)."
          - list
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Europe: $12.81–38.19 million (determined by a ranking based on sporting and commercial criteria)"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "South America: $15.21 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "North, Central America & Caribbean: $9.55 million"

              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Asia: $9.55 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Africa: $9.55 million"
            - listitem [level=1]
              - ListMarker "• "
              - StaticText "Oceania: $3.58 million"
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "Solidarity payments (US$250 million):"
            - StaticText " In addition to the prize money for the participating teams, these payments were allocated to support clubs worldwide, fostering development and inclusivity in global football."
        - region "Broadcasting" [ref=e27]
          - generic
            - heading "Broadcasting" [level=2, ref=e202]
            - link "edit" [ref=e203]
          - paragraph
            - StaticText "In July 2024, FIFA opened bids for media rights to the Club World Cup in the Americas, Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. It was reported that "
            - link "Apple" [ref=e204]
            - StaticText " (owner of the global rights to "
            - link "Major League Soccer" [ref=e205]
            - StaticText ") had attempted to make a $1 billion bid for global rights to the 2025 Club World Cup, but negotiations with FIFA had reportedly stalled; the bid was said to be a quarter of what FIFA had targeted for the rights to the tournament."

              - link "[118]" [ref=e425]

            - link "Warner Bros. Discovery" [ref=e207]

            - superscript

          - region "Impact of multi-club ownership" [ref=e80]
            - generic
              - heading "Impact of multi-club ownership" [level=3, ref=e475]
              - link "edit" [ref=e476]
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "Several clubs in the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup were linked to multi-club ownership structures, raising concerns about conflicts of interest. Among them were Mexican sides "
              - link "Pachuca" [ref=e477]
              - StaticText " and "
              - link "León" [ref=e478]
              - StaticText ", both owned by Grupo Pachuca. FIFA regulations prohibit any club from owning shares in, being a member of, or exerting influence over another participating club, with \"influence\" defined through control of voting rights or decision-making authority."
              - superscript
                - link "[34]" [ref=e1864]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "34"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " In November 2024, Costa Rican club "
              - link "Alajuelense" [ref=e479]
              - StaticText " requested FIFA to apply this rule and disqualify one of the two Grupo Pachuca clubs, threatening legal action if no action was taken."
              - superscript
                - link "[259]" [ref=e1865]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "259"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " Alajuelense argued that it was next in line to qualify under CONCACAF's rankings, but FIFA determined the club could not be party to proceedings."
              - superscript
                - link "[260]" [ref=e1866]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "260"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " On February 4, 2025, Alajuelense appealed to the "
              - link "Court of Arbitration for Sport" [ref=e480]
              - StaticText " against FIFA, Pachuca, and León."
              - superscript
                - link "[261]" [ref=e1867]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "261"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " On March 21, FIFA announced that León had been removed from the tournament."

                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "262"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " According to "

              - link "Los Angeles FC" [ref=e481]
              - StaticText ", runner-up of the 2023 CONCACAF Champions League, and "
              - link "América" [ref=e482]
              - StaticText ", the highest-ranked Mexican club not already qualified."

            - generic
              - heading "Weather and logistical challenges" [level=3, ref=e529]
              - link "edit" [ref=e530]
            - paragraph
              - StaticText "The tournament was marked by significant weather-related and logistical disruptions, raising concerns ahead of the "
              - link "2026 FIFA World Cup" [ref=e531]
              - StaticText ". Several matches were delayed or temporarily suspended due to "
              - link "thunderstorms" [ref=e532]
              - StaticText " and "
              - link "lightning" [ref=e533]
              - StaticText ", with stoppages ranging from around 46 minutes to nearly two hours, as FIFA safety protocols required repeated pauses whenever lightning was detected near stadiums."
              - superscript
                - link "[297]" [ref=e1913]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "297"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " High temperatures also posed a challenge, particularly for midday kickoffs, with players and coaches highlighting the physical toll of extreme heat and uneven playing conditions between day and evening matches."
              - superscript
                - link "[298]" [ref=e1914]
                  - generic
                    - StaticText "["
                    - StaticText "298"
                    - StaticText "]"
              - StaticText " Beyond the pitch, severe weather contributed to travel and traffic problems, including flight delays and congestion around venues, affecting teams, officials, media, and supporters, further intensifying debate about scheduling and infrastructure preparedness for future tournaments."
